sections.text:
The growing volume of process data generated by screwdriving systems, combined with advancements in computing power, data storage, and algorithms, is facilitating the application of artificial intelligence in this field.

Accurately detecting and classifying screwdriving errors is crucial for ensuring product quality, avoiding costly rework in manufacturing, and supporting sustainability by facilitating the maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products.

In this context, machine learning approaches offer a promising alternative to traditional monitoring techniques, such as window-based methods or envelope curves. This study examines the use of deep learning techniques for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving processes.

The data corpus consists of multivariate time series capturing process parameters, such as torque and rotation angle. For anomaly detection, the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder was analyzed. In terms of error classification, four different model architectures were evaluated.

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection and confirm that deep learning models can distinguish between multiple error categories beyond traditional binary classification. This extends the capabilities of conventional monitoring approaches, achieving accuracies of up to 100%.

Additionally, real-world data material was examined in order to further demonstrate model robustness.

Overall the results indicate strong generalization capability and highlight the practical potential of the developed models for use in industrial screwdriving processes, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in error identification and significantly reducing manual effort and analysis time.

summary.en: This study examines deep learning for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving, using multivariate time series such as torque and rotation angle. Anomaly detection analyzes the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder, while error classification evaluates four model architectures. The authors report effective anomaly detection and discrimination among multiple error categories, with accuracy reaching up to 100%. They also examine real-world data to investigate robustness and describe the results as indicating strong generalization and practical industrial potential.
summary.zh: 本文研究深度学习在螺钉拧紧过程异常检测与错误分类中的应用，使用包含扭矩、旋转角度等过程参数的多变量时间序列。异常检测分析了向量量化变分自编码器的嵌入空间；错误分类比较了四种模型架构。作者报告，异常检测有效，模型能够区分多类错误，准确率最高达到100%，并使用真实世界数据考察稳健性。研究称结果显示出较强泛化能力及工业应用潜力，可减少错误识别对专家知识的依赖以及人工分析工作和时间。

sections.text:
Nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) enables highly performant control of constrained systems, but its computational cost prohibits real-time use on fast dynamical systems.

Neural network imitation of the TOMPC control law can reduce online computational costs, yet existing work mostly targets quadratic cost formulations in simulation and addresses the challenges of neural controllers in isolation.

This work imitates a long-horizon nonconvex TOMPC with hard terminal constraints, whose high computational cost limits training-data generation.

We present (i) \emph{self-informed sampling (SIFS)}, a data-efficient expert-sampling strategy that uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert only where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior, (ii) a complete training and control architecture that jointly addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal expert labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction and model mismatch, and (iii) real-world validation on a Furuta pendulum.

SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz.

On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.

summary.en: This work imitates long-horizon, nonconvex time-optimal model predictive control with hard terminal constraints. Its self-informed sampling strategy uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior. The training and control architecture also addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction, and model mismatch. The authors report matching standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the data. On a real Furuta pendulum, the controller raises frequency from 1.4 Hz to 1 kHz while closely matching expert trajectories.
summary.zh: 本文针对长时域、非凸且带硬终端约束的非线性时间最优模型预测控制，提出神经网络模仿方案。自我提示采样（SIFS）利用学习到的剩余时间，仅在策略偏离时间最优行为处查询专家；整体架构还处理数据相关性、次优专家标签、协变量偏移、约束满足和模型失配。作者报告，SIFS约用三分之一训练时间、不到一半训练数据，即达到标准数据集聚合的表现。最终控制器匹配专家的吸引域，并在真实 Furuta 摆验证中将控制频率从1.4 Hz提高到1 kHz，摆起和稳定轨迹接近专家方案。

sections.text:
Many manipulation tasks require separating adhered, embedded, contaminated, or mechanically constrained targets. We study this setting as removal manipulation, where progress depends on evolving contact states that are only partially observable from vision and kinematics.

We introduce DexRemo, a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation, modular fingertips, and three-axis fingertip force sensing, together with a nine-scenario real-robot task suite spanning adhesive detachment, surface cleaning and self-cleaning, and occluded retrieval.

To make multi-finger force observations easier to fuse, we express fingertip forces in a shared wrist-centered frame, giving force components consistent geometric meaning across fingers and time.

Using an Action Chunking Transformer backbone, policies fuse multi-view vision, proprioception, fingertip pose, and force observations to predict closed-loop action chunks from demonstrations. Evaluation uses six core benchmark tasks for controlled fingertip-input and force-frame ablations, plus three extension scenarios for additional held-out coverage.

Across these evaluations, the learned policies achieve consistent removal performance, and ablations show that wrist-frame forces, especially with fingertip pose, improve stability and generalization over local-frame force inputs and no-force baselines. Project website: https://dexremo.github.io

summary.en: The authors introduce DexRemo, a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation, modular fingertips, and three-axis fingertip force sensing, alongside nine real-robot removal scenarios. Fingertip forces are represented in a shared wrist-centered frame. Policies based on an Action Chunking Transformer combine multi-view vision, proprioception, fingertip pose, and force observations to predict closed-loop action chunks from demonstrations. Evaluation covers six core benchmark tasks and three extension scenarios. The authors report consistent removal performance and find that wrist-frame forces, especially when combined with fingertip pose, improve stability and generalization over the stated baselines.

summary.en: The paper presents REIS, a human cognition inspired robotic decision framework designed to reduce temporal redundancy in reasoning workloads, where consecutive observations can yield identical actions and subgoals. It combines lightweight scene gating, KV-steered affordance routing, and deliberative reasoning to accelerate control under embodied constraints. Experiments on ALFRED and real-world robotic tasks are reported to show reduced reasoning overhead while maintaining competitive task performance.

sections.text:
Industrial manipulators offer reach and precision but can damage nearby structures in confined spaces. Soft robots provide compliant contact but typically have limited reach. Rigid-soft systems combine their advantages, although they often require dedicated actuation and control hardware.

We propose actuating a passive tendon-driven soft extension through manipulator joint motion. As the robot moves, the exterior spans of tendons anchored to upstream links change, altering tendon tension and deforming the extension. Inspection through narrow apertures, for example, constrains the motion of the end effector (EE).

We develop a controller that regulates the soft tip while preserving such EE constraints. A differential model separates rigid transport from soft deformation, combining analytic arm and tendon kinematics with a locally identified span-to-deformation map.

We also derive a local upper bound on the number of independent deformation directions transmitted by the tendons under the EE constraint, and conditions for the exponential convergence of the tip error. A quadratic program with control barrier functions imposes obstacle clearance, fulcrum limits, and model-validity conditions.

Simulations and real experiments show tip and shape regulation under free, position-constrained, and fulcrum-constrained EE motion.

summary.en: The paper proposes driving a passive tendon-driven soft extension through the motion of a rigid manipulator’s joints. Changes in tendon spans alter tension and deform the extension. For tasks that constrain end-effector motion, the authors develop a controller to regulate the soft tip while preserving those constraints, supported by a differential model separating rigid transport from soft deformation. They derive a bound on transmitted deformation directions and conditions for exponential tip-error convergence. Simulations and real experiments demonstrate tip and shape regulation under several motion constraints.
summary.zh: 论文提出利用机械臂关节运动驱动被动腱绳软延伸段，使机械臂运动改变腱绳张力并带动软段变形。针对狭窄空间检查等限制末端执行器运动的情形，作者设计控制器，在维持末端约束的同时调节软端，并建立区分刚性搬运与软变形的微分模型。研究还推导末端约束下腱绳可传递的独立变形方向上界及误差指数收敛条件，并用带控制屏障函数的二次规划施加安全约束。仿真和真实实验展示了自由、位置受限及支点受限运动下的端部与形状调节。

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown great promise for robotic manipulation by mapping multi-modal semantics to physical actions. However, this mapping inherently struggles to align these coarse-grained semantics with fine-grained temporal execution.

It leaves VLA models with limited generalization and insufficient robustness in cluttered environments. To overcome this issue, we propose ActionUNet, an efficient multi-scale fine-tuning framework that enhances pre-trained VLA models with minimal computational cost.

ActionUNet first constructs a lightweight temporal U-Net within the temporal-aligned action feature space to fuse hierarchical structural priors, effectively bridging the scale gap between semantics and temporal executions.

Recognizing that multi-scale modeling can disrupt microscopic temporal continuity and cause mechanical oscillations, ActionUNet then employs a conditional SIREN as a continuous action decoder. Equipped with explicit second-order smoothness constraints, this decoder guarantees temporal continuity and reduces high-frequency motion jitter.

By smoothing temporal discontinuities from multi-scale fusion, this continuous formulation reduces mechanical execution failures while preserving the base VLA model's generalization and manipulation robustness.

Extensive experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks, together with real-world hard evaluations, demonstrate that ActionUNet significantly improves {\pi}0.5 success rates by absolute 9.8%, 6.1%, and 11.4%, respectively, while also generalizing to the regression-based OpenVLA-OFT backbone, highlighting its effectiveness and efficiency as a fine-tuning strategy.

Code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/Di-Zhu123/ActionUNet.

summary.en: The paper introduces ActionUNet, a low-compute fine-tuning framework for pretrained vision-language-action models. It adds a lightweight temporal U-Net to fuse multiscale structure in temporally aligned action features, then uses a conditional SIREN with second-order smoothness constraints to decode continuous actions. The authors say this reduces jitter and execution failures while retaining the base model’s generalization. They report absolute π0.5 success-rate gains of 9.8%, 6.1%, and 11.4% on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO-Plus, and real-world hard evaluations, respectively, and report generalization to OpenVLA-OFT.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ActionUNet，一种以较低计算成本微调预训练视觉—语言—动作模型的方法。它在时间对齐的动作特征空间中加入轻量级时间 U-Net，以融合多尺度结构信息，并使用带二阶平滑约束的条件 SIREN 连续解码动作，旨在减少抖动和执行失败，同时保留基础模型的泛化能力。作者报告称，在 RoboTwin 2.0、LIBERO-Plus 和真实世界困难评测中，π0.5 成功率分别绝对提升 9.8%、6.1% 和 11.4%，并称该方法可推广至 OpenVLA-OFT 骨干模型。

sections.text:
Persistent deformation complicates elasto-plastic manipulation by coupling physical interaction with spatially distributed shape changes. We investigate the force--deformation relationship using a standard robot, a single eye-in-hand RGB-D camera, and intrinsic force estimates.

A 7-DoF Franka Emika FR3 performs normal indentations while an Intel RealSense L515 captures pre- and post-contact surfaces. Point-cloud processing localizes deformation and estimates displaced volume. Force--volume characterization includes 27 measurements over nine force levels.

A compact multilayer perceptron (MLP), trained on 52 force--volume pairs at four levels, achieves a held-out RMSE of 1.857 N and $R^2=0.440$.A separate comparison shows lower error for a quadratic model at 16 N and for the MLP at 19 and 23.5 N.

An eight-step experiment at 4 N per interaction demonstrates cumulative deformation localization from the second indentation onward. These results establish a practical measurement basis for deformation-aware manipulation using intrinsic force estimates and single-view geometry.

summary.en: The paper studies the relationship between force and persistent deformation during manipulation of elasto-plastic materials, using a standard robot, a single eye-in-hand RGB-D camera, and intrinsic force estimates. Normal indentations and pre- and post-contact point clouds are used to localize deformation and estimate displaced volume. The authors report that an MLP trained on 52 force-volume pairs has a held-out RMSE of 1.857 N and an R² of 0.440; a separate comparison finds lower error for a quadratic model at one force level and for the MLP at two others. An eight-step experiment localizes cumulative deformation from the second indentation onward.
summary.zh: 论文研究弹塑性材料操作中的力与永久形变关系，使用标准机器人、单个手眼 RGB-D 相机和机器人自身的力估计。研究通过法向压入及接触前后表面点云处理来定位形变、估算位移体积，并开展力—体积测量。作者报告，一个以 52 组数据训练的多层感知器在留出数据上的 RMSE 为 1.857 N、R² 为 0.440；不同力级下，二次模型或多层感知器误差较低。另有八步实验显示，从第二次压入起可定位累积形变。

sections.text:
Vision-language models (VLMs) have become a powerful foundation for robotic scene understanding, task planning, and language-conditioned control. A natural question follows: can these models also decode what a human operator intends while teleoperating a robot, without any explicit instruction?

We formulate this as hierarchical intent prediction, jointly inferring the ongoing atomic action and the broader mission it serves from a short visual teleoperation history.

To study this, we introduce VI AMO (Vision Intention Action and Mission Ongoing), a dataset of 6,600 episodes from eleven robot sources with 13,653 temporally aligned action annotations and 9,702 mission annotations.

Large proprietary models struggle with this problem: on held-out episodes, GPT-4o reaches Sentence-BERT similarities of only 0.563 and 0.470 for action and mission, and GPT-5.6 Luna achieves only 0.581 and 0.554.

Fine-tuning a VLM on VI AMO yields our Vision-Intention Model (VIM), which raises these scores to 0.825 and 0.821 and still reaches 0.726 and 0.717 on the 35.4% of test actions with both labels absent from training.

Finally, as a downstream application, VIM's predicted mission enables a vision-language-action (VLA) policy to take over from the operator mid-task in a real-world environment unseen during VIM fine-tuning, reducing human teleoperation time by 34.6% relative to GPT-4o and 39.8% relative to GPT-5.6 Luna, while cutting intent-prediction latency by roughly 70% on average.

summary.en: The paper frames hierarchical intent prediction as inferring both an operator’s ongoing atomic action and its broader mission from a short visual teleoperation history. The authors introduce VI AMO, a dataset of 6,600 episodes from eleven robot sources with aligned action and mission annotations, and fine-tune a vision-language model to create VIM. They report higher action and mission similarity scores than the compared large models, including on test actions whose labels were both absent from training. In a real-world downstream experiment, VIM’s predicted mission lets a VLA policy take over mid-task, reducing teleoperation time and intent-prediction latency.
summary.zh: 论文提出分层意图预测任务：根据短时视觉遥操作历史，同时推断操作员正在执行的原子动作及其所属的更广泛任务。作者构建了 VI AMO 数据集，包含来自 11 个机器人来源的 6,600 段记录及时间对齐的动作、任务标注，并微调视觉语言模型得到 VIM。作者报告，VIM 的动作和任务相似度分数高于所比较的大型模型，在训练中两类标签均未出现的测试动作上也取得相应分数。真实世界下游实验中，VIM 预测的任务使 VLA 策略得以中途接管，并减少遥操作时间及意图预测延迟。

sections.text:
Soft robots built from active materials can directly convert environmental stimuli into motion, offering a route to energy autonomy and embodied control. However, environmental energy is generally harvested at low power, whereas rapid, mechanically demanding actions require high mechanical output power.

Reconciling this mismatch while sustaining self-regulated cyclic actuation is challenging, particularly at the subgram scale, where limited payload capacity constrains the integration of conventional power and control hardware.

Here, we present SunLightBots, a class of subgram, sunlight-powered, untethered soft robots that achieve autonomous locomotion under continuous illumination near 1 Sun (100 mW/cm2).

Their operation is enabled by a self-resetting snapping (SRS) mechanism that integrates liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) with snap-through instability to accumulate solar energy supplied at low power, release it as rapid, high-power motion, and reset through photothermal-mechanical feedback.

Through coordinated optimization of the LCE actuation temperature, photothermal conversion, actuation stress, and structural energy barrier, the system operates near 1 Sun and achieves a peak mass-specific mechanical power of 89 W/kg. At this irradiance, the optimized LCE generates an actuation stress of 0.1 MPa at approximately 60 deg C.

SunLightBots demonstrate sustained swimming, crawling, and repeated impulsive jumping. Under 1.5 Suns, the swimmer advances more than three body lengths per cycle. This work provides a materials-mechanics route toward autonomous soft robots powered entirely by the environment.

summary.en: The paper presents SunLightBots, subgram untethered soft robots that move autonomously under continuous illumination near 1 Sun. Their self-resetting snapping mechanism combines liquid crystal elastomers with snap-through instability to accumulate low-power solar energy, release it as rapid, high-power motion, and reset through photothermal-mechanical feedback. The authors report a peak mass-specific mechanical power of 89 W/kg and demonstrate sustained swimming, crawling, and repeated jumping. At 1.5 Suns, the swimmer advances more than three body lengths per cycle.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 SunLightBots，一类亚克级、无系留的软体机器人，可在接近 1 Sun 的持续照射下自主运动。其自复位弹跳机制结合液晶弹性体与屈曲失稳，将低功率太阳能积累后转化为快速、高功率动作，并通过光热—机械反馈复位。作者报告峰值质量比机械功率为 89 W/kg，并展示持续游动、爬行和重复跳跃；在 1.5 Suns 下，游泳机器人每周期前进超过三个身长。

items.title: SunLightBots: Turning sunlight into self-sustained, high-power motion in soft robots

sections.text:
Coding agents are evaluated mostly on general-purpose software, but domain-specific systems require domain-aware evaluation.

Robot software is a particularly challenging case: Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) packages have their own build tools, simulators and learning frameworks are built on physics engines, and behavior that depends on timing and hardware is hard to test.

We present Robo-SWE, a dataset of 236 executable issue-resolution tasks mined from merged pull requests in 28 public robotics repositories in four domains: ROS 2 systems, simulation and physics engines, robotics algorithm libraries, and robot-learning frameworks.

Each task contains the original issue text, a container recipe for the repository at the commit before the fix, the developers' fix, and the developers' tests, which fail before the fix and pass after it in repeated offline runs.

The dataset also keeps a provenance ledger of all 1,567 candidate pull requests, with the stage each reached and the reason for every rejection, and, as a first use, 3,540 graded attempts by five coding-agent setups with recorded patches and 3,529 available trajectories.

The tasks are validated by execution; verification of their fairness by human reviewers is future work. The dataset and public leaderboard are available online.

It covers ROS 2, simulation and physics engines, robotics algorithm libraries, and robot-learning frameworks. Each task includes the original issue, a pre-fix repository environment, the developers’ fix, and tests that fail before and pass after the fix in repeated offline runs. The authors report coding-agent attempts and resolve rates; execution validates the tasks, while fairness review by humans remains future work.

sections.text:
Humanoid motion tracking is fundamental to reproducing human motions on humanoid robots and serves as an important tool for teleoperation and motion data collection. However, directly tracking reference motions can be unsafe in constrained environments or during physical human--robot interaction, motivating the need for compliant motion tracking.

We present ILA, an Interface-Level Adapter for compliant humanoid motion tracking without dedicated interaction sensors. ILA adapts motion references from the robot's observation history, allowing the robot to respond to physical guidance while preserving the capabilities of a pretrained motion tracker.

As an interface-level module, ILA can be directly plugged into different pretrained motion trackers without retraining either the adapter or the tracking policies. ILA is trained entirely in simulation to predict reference corrections induced by physical interaction.

We evaluate ILA with three humanoid motion trackers and achieve a 63.6--75.4% reduction in guidance-target error compared with their original policies. Matched simulation studies and hardware experiments further show that ILA improves responsiveness to human guidance while preserving nominal motion-tracking performance.

These results demonstrate compliant guidance as a reusable, sensor-free extension to pretrained humanoid motion trackers.

summary.en: The paper presents ILA, an interface-level adapter for compliant humanoid motion tracking without dedicated interaction sensors. Using the robot’s observation history, it adjusts motion references so the robot can respond to physical guidance while retaining a pretrained tracker’s capabilities. The module can be added to different trackers without retraining the adapter or policies, and is trained entirely in simulation. Evaluations with three trackers report a 63.6–75.4% reduction in guidance-target error. Matched simulation studies and hardware experiments show improved responsiveness while preserving nominal tracking performance.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ILA，一种无需专用交互传感器的类人机器人柔顺动作跟踪适配器。它根据机器人观测历史调整动作参考，使机器人能够响应物理引导，同时保留预训练跟踪器的能力；该模块可接入不同跟踪器，无需重新训练适配器或策略。ILA 完全在仿真中训练。作者在三个跟踪器上评估，报告引导目标误差降低 63.6%–75.4%；匹配的仿真研究与硬件实验显示，响应性提升且常规动作跟踪表现得以保持。

sections.text:
For robots to assist, serve, and collaborate with humans, they must not only interpret human requests conveyed through language and multimodal intentional cues, but also execute long-horizon tasks that interleave navigation and manipulation. In this paper, we introduce HEIR, a resource for studying how to Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interaction.

HEIR pairs human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, while each session preserves successive episodes, with each request fulfilled through multiple execution subtasks.

The captured data, together with human-authored annotations, support the study of intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion within a unified interaction setting.

To demonstrate the value of HEIR, we conduct extensive offline experiments to evaluate how models benefit from additional human-centric context across these tasks, together with real-robot experiments that assess execution task completion.

HEIR thus provides a valuable resource for studying user-centric robot interaction in naturalistic household environments. Our demo and dataset are available online.

summary.en: HEIR is a resource for studying human-robot interaction. It pairs human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories. Sessions preserve successive episodes in which a request may involve multiple execution subtasks. The data and human-authored annotations support research on intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion. The authors report offline experiments on human-centric context and real-robot experiments assessing task completion, but the abstract does not specify their results.

sections.text:
Tabletop games offer a compelling scenario to study the interaction between artificial and human agents, combining social interaction with game state tracking and physical manipulation.

To assess the game state, a robot needs to precisely detect closely related game objects, such as different card designs, requiring dedicated training data that is costly to annotate in the real world.

Instead, we develop a fully automated synthetic data collection pipeline, using re-projection of known 3D coordinates to generate labels automatically and domain randomization to bridge the reality gap.

This approach is used to collect a dataset of 25413 samples to finetune an object detection and a segmentation model, which are combined to assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the game state.

When evaluated on a real NICO humanoid robot, our pipeline achieves an F1-score of 0.906 for card-to-zone assignment, thus providing the perceptual foundation for a robot that can autonomously play Chef's Hat against human players.

summary.en: The paper presents an automated synthetic-data pipeline for detecting game state in Chef’s Hat. It generates labels by reprojecting known 3D coordinates and uses domain randomization to bridge the reality gap. The resulting 25,413 samples are used to fine-tune object detection and segmentation models, which assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the state. In evaluation on a real NICO humanoid robot, card-to-zone assignment achieves an F1-score of 0.906.
summary.zh: 本文针对机器人在 Chef’s Hat 卡牌游戏中识别游戏状态的需求，提出全自动合成数据采集流程：通过已知三维坐标的重新投影自动生成标签，并使用域随机化缩小仿真与现实之间的差距。作者利用所得的 25413 个样本微调目标检测和分割模型，再将检测到的卡牌分配到游戏相关区域以推断状态。在 NICO 人形机器人上的真实环境评估中，卡牌区域分配的 F1 分数为 0.906。

sections.text:
Humanoid household manipulation requires the arms to act while the body balances, steps and changes posture. We present BiGym 2.0, an adaptation of BiGym for the Unitree G1 across 20 household tasks using a unified whole-body controller for demonstration and evaluation.

The suite provides 60 native human virtual-reality demonstrations per task with synchronised multi-camera views and full-body execution records. We benchmark vision-language-action fine-tuning, imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning, and cold-start coding agents given the interaction budget of online reinforcement learning.

With the same onboard views, proprioception and whole-body controller for every method, vision-language-action fine-tuning has the highest nine-task mean, and agent-developed programs outperform every demo-driven reinforcement learning baseline on this mean and lead on bimanual reaching.

Cross-workspace stacking remains open, $\pi_{0.5}$ stays low on pick-box, and multi-object transport is hard for imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning and coding agents. All environments, human demonstrations, and evaluation traces are open-sourced at https://github.com/swirl-uk/BiGym2.

summary.en: BiGym 2.0 adapts the BiGym benchmark to the Unitree G1 humanoid, covering 20 household tasks with a unified whole-body controller. It provides 60 native human VR demonstrations per task and compares vision-language-action fine-tuning, imitation learning, demo-driven reinforcement learning, and cold-start coding agents. Under shared onboard views, proprioception, and control, vision-language-action fine-tuning has the highest mean across nine tasks. Agent-developed programs outperform demo-driven reinforcement learning baselines on that mean and lead in bimanual reaching. Cross-workspace stacking remains unsolved, and other tasks remain challenging.

sections.text:
Soft pneumatic actuators are widely used in soft robotics because they can produce large motions while remaining compliant enough to interact safely with objects, environments, and the human body. However, their performance is not solely determined by pressure.

Instead, the response depends on the way the actuator is built, including the shape of its chambers, the placement of reinforcements, the use of folds, material stiffness, and the constraints that guide its deformation.

As the literature has expanded, it has become more difficult to determine which mechanism is most suitable for a given application and which reported results can be compared across studies.

This review examines soft pneumatic actuators according to the design strategies used to generate four motion classes: linear, bending, twisting, and omnidirectional actuation.

For each class, it analyzes the structural features that define the deformation path, including braid angle, fold geometry, fiber orientation, chamber arrangement, structural asymmetry, and internal constraint layers.

It then discusses how the design choice affect motion output, force generation, air demand, repeatability, durability, fabrication difficulty, and robotic integration.

The review further identifies key conditions that must be considered when selecting or comparing actuators, including pressure, loading condition, actuator size, pneumatic supply, and hysteresis This approach helps explain why actuators with similar motion outputs may differ substantially in design requirements, pneumatic demand, and practical suitability.

It also highlights the design priorities needed for compact, efficient, repeatable, and deployable soft pneumatic systems in wearable, biomedical, and mobile robotic applications.

summary.en: This review organizes soft pneumatic actuators by four motion classes: linear, bending, twisting, and omnidirectional. It examines how features such as chamber arrangement, reinforcement, folds, fiber orientation, asymmetry, and internal constraints shape deformation. The review discusses effects on motion, force, air demand, repeatability, durability, fabrication, and integration, and identifies pressure, loading, size, pneumatic supply, and hysteresis as comparison and selection conditions. It highlights design priorities for wearable, biomedical, and mobile robotic applications.
summary.zh: 本文综述软体气动执行器如何通过结构设计产生直线、弯曲、扭转和全向运动，分析腔体形状、增强结构、折叠、纤维方向及内部约束等因素与变形路径的关系。文章讨论设计对运动、力、耗气量、重复性、耐久性、制造和机器人集成的影响，并指出比较与选型时需考虑压力、负载、尺寸、气源和迟滞。综述强调面向可穿戴、生物医学及移动机器人应用的设计需求。

items.title: Soft Pneumatic Actuators for Robotics: From Motion Generation to Performance Optimization

sections.text:
We introduce CABOT, a computational model for autonomous mobile robots in which the discrete plane the robots operate on is not a passive stage but an active computing medium.

In the classical Look-Compute-Move (LCM) model every increase in computational capability is obtained by strengthening the robots themselves, with lights, memory or wider visibility, at a cost paid once per robot.

CABOT strengthens the environment instead: each cell of the grid holds a state from a finite set Q, the states evolve synchronously under a uniform local rule that also senses whether a robot stands on the cell, that is, the floor is a cellular automaton, and the Look operation returns the states of the visible cells in addition to the positions of the visible robots.

The robots are as weak as we can make them: oblivious, silent, lightless, myopic with visibility range 1, without multiplicity detection and unable to write to the floor. The number of field states |Q|, rather than any robot capability, becomes the measure of the resources required.

On an inert floor (|Q| = 1) such robots can neither form a line, nor gather from scattered positions, nor explore a grid. We show that a handful of states changes this. Line Formation from connected configurations is solvable with four states, and field-silently, so that the floor also reaches a fixed point, with five.

Gathering from arbitrary, possibly disconnected, configurations is solvable with three states and Line Formation from arbitrary configurations with six; we prove that neither can be solved field-silently with any number of states. A single robot explores every finite grid forever with four states and every torus with two, which is optimal.

Further rule sets, validated by simulation only, equalize the spacing of robots on a row, fill a pattern painted on the floor and guide robots through a maze, and indicate the range of the model.

summary.en: The paper introduces CABOT, a model in which grid cells form an active computing field whose finite states evolve synchronously under a local rule. Robots are oblivious, lightless, have visibility range one, and cannot write to the field. The authors establish state requirements and solvability results for line formation, gathering, and exploration, including impossibility results for field-silent solutions to some tasks. Additional rule sets for spacing, pattern filling, and maze guidance are validated by simulation only.
summary.zh: 本文提出 CABOT 模型，把网格环境视为主动计算介质：每个格子具有有限状态，并按统一局部规则同步演化；机器人则保持无记忆、无灯、视距为一且不能写入地面的弱能力。作者给出不同任务所需状态数及可解性结果，包括成线、聚集和探索，并证明部分任务不能以场静默方式完成。另有规则集仅经仿真验证，用于均匀间距、填充图案和迷宫导航。

However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction. sections.text:
Conventional vector-field-based motion planners for nonholonomic robots consist of two steps: first designing a nominal vector field and then controlling the robot to follow it to approach the target.

However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction.

This paper proposes a diffeomorphic vector-field alignment (DIVAL) method, which aligns the vector field's direction with the robot's initial heading so the robot can follow the vector field from the start.

Specifically, the nominal vector field is locally reshaped by applying a diffeomorphic deformation to the workspace, such that the reshaped vector field has the same direction as the robot's heading at the initial position and coincides with the nominal vector field outside the deformed region.

Since DIVAL eliminates the initial heading mismatch, the nonholonomic robot can maintain heading alignment with the reshaped vector field throughout the motion. This heading alignment further ensures that the robot preserves the nominal vector field's properties, including obstacle avoidance, convergence to the target, and smooth control signals.

Numerical simulations provide vector-field-tracking baselines where the nominal vector fields are reshaped with DIVAL. Compared to the original baselines, the proposed method achieves collision-free convergence in all trials and avoids control discontinuities.

Hardware experiments on a ground vehicle further demonstrate collision-free convergence across different targets and initial conditions under real-world disturbances.

summary.en: The paper proposes DIVAL, which locally deforms a nominal vector field so its direction matches a nonholonomic robot’s initial heading while retaining the nominal field outside the deformed region. The authors state that this alignment lets the robot follow the field from the start while preserving obstacle avoidance, target convergence, and smooth control. In numerical simulations, the method achieved collision-free convergence in all trials and avoided control discontinuities. Ground-vehicle hardware experiments demonstrated collision-free convergence across targets and initial conditions under real-world disturbances.
summary.zh: 本文提出 DIVAL，通过对工作空间施加局部微分同胚变形，使名义向量场在机器人初始位置与其朝向一致，并在变形区域外保持原场。作者称这种对齐可消除初始航向不匹配，使非完整约束机器人跟随变形后的向量场，同时保留避障、目标收敛和控制平滑等性质。数值仿真显示所有试验均无碰撞并收敛，且避免控制不连续；地面车辆硬件实验则在扰动下展示不同目标和初始条件中的无碰撞收敛。

items.title: DIVAL: Diffeomorphic Vector-Field Alignment for Nonholonomic Motion Planning

sections.text:
Generating diverse robot videos requires control over scene geometry, robot motion, and viewpoints. End-to-end video generation offers limited direct access to these variables, making targeted edits and reuse across tasks difficult. We present BWM-Forge, a code-driven framework for controllable video generation in robotics.

Given robot assets and a task description, the framework accepts an initial image, an image with motion data, or a human demonstration video. A coding agent constructs editable Blender scene programs that specify objects, robot motion, and cameras.

The resulting proxy videos provide structural and motion references for a video generation model, which adds visual detail. A multi-agent harness coordinates input processing, scene construction, review, and rendering.

Automated evaluation and user feedback support iterative refinement, while an experience repository stores and retrieves reusable modeling and rendering rules. This design supports multiple robot embodiments, synchronized viewpoints, and appearance variation from a shared scene program. We evaluate the framework on 15 tasks covering five robot types.

Compared with LingBot-World Base Cam on these tasks, BWM-Forge achieves higher aesthetic quality, imaging quality, subject and background consistency, motion smoothness, and RoboJudge-9B physical adherence and instruction alignment scores. The baseline scores higher in dynamic degree.

Qualitative cases illustrate viewpoint control, scene variation, feedback-driven edits, and experience reuse across scenes. These results demonstrate a practical approach to generating controllable robot videos through editable, executable scene representations.

summary.en: BWM-Forge is a code-driven framework for controllable robot video generation using editable Blender scene programs. Given robot assets and a task description, it can accept an initial image, motion-data image, or human demonstration video. A coding agent specifies objects, robot motion, and cameras; proxy videos then guide a video model’s visual rendering. The framework supports multiple embodiments, synchronized viewpoints, and appearance variation. Evaluation across 15 tasks and five robot types found higher scores than LingBot-World Base Cam on several quality, consistency, smoothness, and RoboJudge-9B measures, while the baseline scored higher in dynamic degree.
summary.zh: 本文介绍 BWM-Forge，一种通过可编辑 Blender 场景程序生成可控机器人视频的代码驱动框架。给定机器人资产和任务描述，系统可接收初始图像、带运动数据的图像或人类演示视频，由编码代理构建描述物体、机器人运动和相机的场景；代理视频再为视频生成模型提供结构与运动参考。框架支持多种机器人、同步视角和外观变化，并以 15 项任务、五类机器人评估。与 LingBot-World Base Cam 相比，其多项画质、一致性、动作平滑度及 RoboJudge-9B 指标更高，但动态程度得分较低。

items.title: BWM-Forge: Agentic World Programming for Embodied Intelligence

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising capabilities for robot manipulation, but their performance on accessible mobile bimanual platforms remains underexplored. We present a low-cost and reproducible mobile bimanual platform integrating two LeRobot SO-101 manipulators with a TurtleBot 4 and a LeRobot-ROS 2 software stack.

Using long-horizon toilet cleaning as a case study, we collect 250 real-world demonstrations and evaluate $\pi_0$, $\pi_{0.5}$, SmolVLA, and GR00T under the same embodiment and task conditions. We further evaluate variants using SARM-derived task-progress signals and short-term MEM observation history.

Among the evaluated models, $\pi_0$ performs best, achieving 60% strict and 70% relaxed autonomous success, increasing to 90% with limited human intervention. In contrast, the evaluated progress- and memory-augmented variants do not improve their corresponding baselines.

Our results demonstrate the feasibility of long-horizon mobile bimanual manipulation on accessible hardware while highlighting remaining challenges in reliable VLA deployment. Project website: https://so101-turtlebot4.github.io/mobile-bimanual-cleaning/

summary.en: This paper presents a low-cost, reproducible mobile bimanual platform combining two LeRobot SO-101 arms, a TurtleBot 4, and a LeRobot-ROS 2 stack. Using long-horizon toilet cleaning as a case study, the authors collect 250 real-world demonstrations and evaluate several VLA models, including variants with task-progress signals or short-term observation history. They report that π₀ performs best, with 60% strict and 70% relaxed autonomous success, rising to 90% with limited human intervention. The augmented variants do not outperform their baselines.
summary.zh: 本文介绍一种低成本、可复现的移动双臂平台，由两台 LeRobot SO-101 机械臂、TurtleBot 4 和 LeRobot-ROS 2 软件栈组成，并以长时程马桶清洁为案例。研究采集了250次真实演示，在相同平台和任务条件下评估多个 VLA 模型及加入任务进度信号或短期观测记忆的变体。作者报告，π₀表现最佳，自主成功率为严格标准60%、宽松标准70%，有限人工介入后为90%；加入进度或记忆的变体未优于相应基线。结果展示了该平台上的可行性，也指出可靠部署仍有挑战。

sections.text:
Most humanoid loco-manipulation controllers require human motion data to learn whole-body coordination and posture, leaving policies reliant on external sources to provide this data.

We present OCLO (Online-posture Compliant LOco-manipulation), a humanoid loco-manipulation system trained without human motion data and commanded only through two end-effector targets and a walking velocity.

Because these targets do not uniquely determine whole-body posture, OCLO generates pelvis height and torso orientation online using an analytic reachability prior, further refined through policy-in-the-loop sampling with a task-agnostic cost.

OCLO also learns whole-body compliance by displacing end-effector references according to measured forces through a spring-damper model, encouraging the legs, waist, and pelvis to yield to external loads.

In simulation, using the reachability prior leads to a 77.8% success rate in acquiring the commanded reference, a vast improvement over the 37.8% success rate accomplished without the prior. Further, refinement reduces end-effector orientation error across all evaluated tasks. The same posture module improves a pretrained SONIC controller on all five tasks.

Without compliance training, policies tend to lose balance under disturbances rather than sacrifice tracking. On a Unitree G1, OCLO maintains balance under end-effector disturbances that cause its ablations to fail and performs nine loco-manipulation tasks, including crouched walking and picking up a box from a low surface.

Project website: https://oclo-humanoid.github.io/

summary.en: The paper introduces OCLO, a humanoid loco-manipulation system trained without human motion data and commanded through two end-effector targets and walking velocity. It generates pelvis height and torso orientation online using an analytic reachability prior, refined through policy-in-the-loop sampling, and learns whole-body compliance by shifting end-effector references in response to measured forces. In simulation, the prior achieves a 77.8% success rate in acquiring commanded references, compared with 37.8% without it; refinement lowers end-effector orientation error across evaluated tasks. On a Unitree G1, the system maintains balance under end-effector disturbances and performs nine loco-manipulation tasks.
summary.zh: 本文提出 OCLO，一种不依赖人体动作数据训练的人形机器人移动操作系统，仅通过两个末端执行器目标和行走速度接受指令。系统利用解析可达性先验在线生成骨盆高度和躯干姿态，并以策略闭环采样进一步调整；还依据测得的外力，通过弹簧阻尼模型移动末端参考点来学习全身柔顺性。仿真中，加入可达性先验后，达到指令参考的成功率为77.8%，不使用先验时为37.8%；姿态调整降低了所测任务的末端方向误差。实机 Unitree G1 测试中，系统能在末端受扰时保持平衡，并完成九项移动操作任务。

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation.

A larger backbone therefore directly blocks reactivity, especially in humanoid dexterous manipulation. We present DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling.

DASH splits the policy into a slow vision-language model (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) that run as concurrent processes over the LCM communication protocol, so the control rate is set by the action head alone, independent of backbone size.

The action head fuses stale semantics from a frozen backbone with fresh vision from its own ResNet encoder, desynchronized training exposes it to the staleness it meets at deployment, and an adaptive temporal aggregator aligns overlapping action chunks under variable inference latency.

On an asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark that charges inference latency in simulated time, DASH holds 20 Hz control rate from 0.8B to 8B backbones while the synchronous rate falls from 9.7 to 4.1 Hz, with higher success at every size. On a real humanoid with dexterous hands, DASH achieves clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.

summary.en: The paper presents DASH, which separates a vision-language model from a fast action head running concurrently, so the action head determines the control rate. Fresh visual input, training for observation staleness, and adaptive temporal aggregation address latency. On an asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark that charges inference latency in simulated time, DASH maintains a 20 Hz control rate across backbone sizes, while the synchronous rate declines, and DASH has higher success at each size. The authors also report clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline on a real humanoid with dexterous hands.
summary.zh: 本文提出 DASH，将视觉语言模型与快速动作头拆分为并发进程，使控制频率由动作头决定，并通过新鲜视觉、针对观测陈旧性的训练及自适应时间聚合处理延迟。在计入推理延迟的异步 RoboTwin 仿真基准中，DASH 使用不同规模骨干网络时维持 20 Hz 控制，同步方案频率下降，且各规模下成功率更高。作者还报告，真实人形机器人灵巧手任务中，DASH 的抓取放置成功率明显高于同步方案。

sections.text:
Model-based planners that roll out imagined futures assume the transition model faithfully propagates task-relevant signals---a property rarely measured directly.

In a single-seed case study of a Recurrent State Space Model world model with active-inference planning in the CARLA driving simulator, we identify a \textbf{posterior-prior gap}---posterior (observation-filtered) states retain obstacle information that imagined rollout states progressively lose: a supervised obstacle probe achieves AUC 0.85 on posterior states, but the same probe applied to imagined prior states shows monotonic decay (AUC 0.85$\rightarrow$0.71 over 15 steps; logit separation drops 57\%).

Because the probe is identical, the decay isolates the transition model---not the representation---as the information bottleneck.

Obstacle avoidance drops to 0\% without privileged runtime coordinates, and the planner's own ensemble-based epistemic term does not flag the loss---ensemble disagreement yields AUC 0.52 as an obstacle classifier (chance level), making the failure an unflagged imagination failure---an unknown unknown at planning time.

As a secondary contribution, we show that \textbf{task-conditioned weighting of Effective Free Energy components} over the same world model yields lane keeping ($81.2 \pm 1.8$\% route completion) and obstacle avoidance (28/28 avoided, \emph{using privileged coordinates}) in the CARLA simulator, with runtime weight modulation enabling post-evasion centering.

summary.en: In a single-seed CARLA driving-simulator case study, the paper finds that observation-filtered posterior states retain obstacle information while imagined rollout prior states progressively lose it. Results from the same probe are presented as evidence that the transition model is the information bottleneck. Without privileged runtime coordinates, obstacle avoidance falls to zero, and the ensemble-based epistemic term does not flag the information loss. As a secondary result, task-conditioned Effective Free Energy weights support lane keeping and obstacle avoidance, though the reported obstacle-avoidance result uses privileged coordinates.
summary.zh: 本文在 CARLA 驾驶仿真的单随机种子案例中，发现世界模型的观测过滤后验状态保留障碍物信息，而想象 rollout 的先验状态逐步丢失该信息；相同探针的结果被用来指出转移模型是信息瓶颈。无特权运行时坐标时，避障率降至零，集成不确定性项也未能提示信息损失。作为次要结果，作者报告任务条件化的有效自由能权重可实现车道保持与避障，但所述避障结果使用了特权坐标。

sections.text:
Long-term spacecraft autonomy requires embodied agents to use operational history under communication delays, time-critical operations, environmental uncertainty, complex physical interactions, power and computational constraints, and safety and reliability requirements.

We introduce AstroMemBench and a Scenario-Challenge-Capability design method that maps these requirements to executable memory tests. The benchmark covers 16 memory subchallenges through 140 templates and 2240 instances across nine tasks in planetary surface operations, on-orbit servicing, and deep-space exploration.

A deterministic environment scores actions for task completion, state changes, safety, and resource use. Ablations under nine conditions show that the benchmark is sensitive to how accurately agents recover and use historical information and to differences in memory-system design. Main experiments compare six configurations.

Mem0, Chain-of-Memory, LightMem, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improve same-session mean scores over native Pi Agent, with no clear advantage of the three memory systems over RAG. After a session restart, Mem0 outperforms RAG by 12.25 points. Benefits favor instruction retention and result reuse over ongoing state tracking and energy reservation.

AstroMemBench supports the design, development, and selection of memory systems for embodied spacecraft agents. AstroMemBench 1.0 and its evaluation code are publicly available: https://github.com/flyingView/AstroMemBench-v1.

summary.en: The paper introduces AstroMemBench, an executable benchmark for testing how embodied spacecraft agents recover and use operational history across planetary surface, on-orbit servicing, and deep-space tasks. A deterministic environment scores task completion, state changes, safety, and resource use. Ablations indicate sensitivity to historical-information use and memory-system design. In the main experiments, several memory systems and retrieval-augmented generation improve same-session mean scores. After a session restart, Mem0 scores higher than RAG. Benefits favor instruction retention and result reuse over ongoing state tracking and energy reservation.
summary.zh: 本文介绍 AstroMemBench，用可执行记忆测试评估具身航天器代理对历史信息的恢复与使用，覆盖地表作业、在轨服务和深空探索任务。确定性环境按任务完成、状态变化、安全和资源使用评分。消融实验显示基准对历史信息使用准确度及记忆系统设计差异敏感。主要实验中，多种记忆系统和检索增强生成提升同一会话平均分；会话重启后，Mem0 得分高于 RAG。收益更偏向指令保留和结果复用，而非持续状态跟踪与能源预留。

items.title: AstroMemBench: A Benchmark for Memory Systems in Embodied Spacecraft Agents

sections.text:
Long-horizon manipulation under uncertainty remains a challenging problem in robotics.

We present \ourmethod{}, an algorithm for Visibility-Aware Task and Motion Planning. \ourmethod{} extends existing deterministic task and motion planning solvers to partially observable object rearrangement tasks, while still being able to take advantage of the efficiency and compositional generalization over long horizons of the base solver.

This extension interleaves sensing actions into a plan skeleton that assumed full observability, and uses a novel persistent object-based memory to fuse observations into object mesh hypotheses and an observed occupancy map.

We evaluate \ourmethod{} on real-world tabletop rearrangement tasks which feature heavy occlusion and partial visibility and demonstrate that it outperforms baselines that do not perform active perception or have persistent memory.

summary.en: The paper presents a visibility-aware task and motion planning algorithm that extends deterministic planners to partially observable object rearrangement. It interleaves sensing actions with a plan skeleton originally designed for full observability, and uses persistent object-based memory to combine observations into object mesh hypotheses and an observed occupancy map. In real-world tabletop rearrangement tasks with heavy occlusion and partial visibility, the authors report better performance than baselines without active perception or persistent memory.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种面向可见性的任务与运动规划算法，将确定性规划求解器扩展到部分可观测的物体重排任务。方法在原本假设完全可观测的计划骨架中交错加入感知动作，并通过持久化的物体级记忆融合观测，形成物体网格假设与已观测占据图。作者在存在严重遮挡和局部可见性的真实桌面重排任务上评估该方法，报告其优于未采用主动感知或持久记忆的基线。

sections.text:
Industrial manipulation requires precise alignment and controlled handling of rigid, deformable, and flexible components. Yet, the benefits of pretrained visuomotor policies remain underexplored in settings where limited access to specialized hardware, components, and fixtures constrains demonstration collection and evaluation.

Understanding task-specific data requirements is important for assessing their scalability across diverse processes on the factory floor. We investigate whether video pretraining can support reliable industrial manipulation with limited action data.

We propose FLUX-mimic, a video-action model, motivated by the potential of video pretraining to capture motion and interaction patterns that enable sample-efficient training. FLUX-mimic is built on a backbone pretrained on large-scale web and industrial task data, and an action expert to generate robot trajectories.

We train our policy by joint video-action training. Across four automotive manufacturing benchmark tasks and two bimanual robot platforms, FLUX-mimic outperforms all considered baselines on the dexterous robot platform and matches pi_{0.5}'s average success rate on the gripper-based robot platform.

On a deformable part kitting task, FLUX-mimic reaches 77.5% success with as little as two hours of task-specific action-labeled demonstrations.

summary.en: The paper investigates whether video pretraining can support reliable industrial manipulation with limited action data and proposes FLUX-mimic, a video-action model. It combines a backbone pretrained on large-scale web and industrial task data with an action expert that generates robot trajectories, and trains the policy jointly on video and action. Across four automotive manufacturing benchmark tasks and two bimanual robot platforms, the authors report that it outperforms considered baselines on the dexterous platform and matches pi_{0.5}'s average success rate on the gripper-based platform. On deformable part kitting, it reaches 77.5% success using two hours of task-specific action-labeled demonstrations.
summary.zh: 本文研究视频预训练能否在动作数据有限时支持可靠的工业操作，并提出视频动作模型 FLUX-mimic。该模型以大规模网络及工业任务数据预训练的骨干网络为基础，并加入生成机器人轨迹的动作专家，通过视频与动作联合训练策略。在四项汽车制造基准任务和两个双臂机器人平台上，作者报告其在灵巧机器人平台上优于所有纳入比较的基线，在夹爪机器人平台上的平均成功率与 pi_{0.5} 相当。变形零件装箱任务中，使用两小时带动作标注的任务示范达到 77.5% 成功率。

items.title: Video-Action Models for Data-Efficient Industrial Manipulation

sections.text:
Probabilistic Virtual Fixtures (VFs) enable the adaptive selection of the most suitable haptic feedback for each phase of a task, based on learned or perceived uncertainty. While keeping the human in the loop remains essential, for instance, to ensure high precision, partial automation of certain task phases is critical for productivity.

We present a unified framework for probabilistic VFs that seamlessly switches between manual fixtures, semi-automated fixtures (with the human handling precise tasks), and full autonomy.

We introduce a novel probabilistic Dynamical System-based VF for coarse guidance, enabling the robot to autonomously complete certain task phases while keeping the human operator in the loop.

For tasks requiring precise guidance, we extend probabilistic position-based trajectory fixtures with automation, allowing for seamless human interaction, geometry-awareness and optimal impedance gains. For manual tasks requiring very precise guidance, we also extend visual servoing fixtures with the same geometry-awareness and impedance behavior.

We validate our approach on different robots, including an evaluation with expert users, showcasing operation modes, the ease of programming fixtures and lower interaction forces and favorable usability compared to a baseline.

summary.en: The paper presents a unified framework for probabilistic virtual fixtures that switches among manual, semi-automated, and autonomous operation based on learned or perceived uncertainty, while retaining a human operator in the loop. A probabilistic dynamical-system fixture provides coarse guidance and allows autonomous completion of some task phases. For precise guidance, the framework extends position-based trajectory fixtures and visual servoing fixtures with automation, geometry awareness, and impedance behavior. Evaluation on different robots, including expert users, reports multiple operating modes, ease of programming, lower interaction forces, and favorable usability compared with a baseline.
summary.zh: 本文提出统一的概率虚拟夹具框架，可依据学习或感知到的不确定性，在手动、半自动和全自主模式间切换，并保留人在环中的角色。框架引入基于动力系统的概率虚拟夹具用于粗略引导，使机器人可自主完成部分任务阶段；对于精确引导，则扩展基于位置的轨迹夹具和视觉伺服夹具，加入自动化、几何感知及阻抗行为。作者在不同机器人上验证方法，并包含专家用户评估，报告展示了多种操作模式、夹具易于编程、交互力较低，且相较基线具有较好的可用性。

sections.text:
Full-size humanoid robots are being considered for hazardous industrial work such as disassembling electric-vehicle batteries. We describe the safety mechanisms of an open-source autonomy stack for the Unitree H1-2 humanoid and what deploying them taught us. All joint commands pass through a safety layer that runs separately from the control software.

It enforces joint position, velocity, and torque limits, and it stops the robot when a state estimate becomes stale or when the hard-wired emergency stop (e-stop) is pressed or disconnected. We pushed the standing robot until it lost balance.

With a model-predictive lower-body controller it never recovered, and the operator had to press the e-stop in every trial. Pressing it removes balance control, and the robot falls. The safety layer's own limits trigger the same stop, and limits chosen for manipulation were exceeded during normal walking.

Near an operator or a battery pack, the fall can be more dangerous than the cause of the stop. Joint limits bound how much force a robot can apply, but not when applying it is appropriate.

Drawing on research on responsibility and on child and adolescent development, we therefore make a case for granting robots force authority in stages, with a person or organization explicitly responsible for its use.

summary.en: The paper describes the safety mechanisms and deployment lessons of an open-source autonomy stack for the Unitree H1-2 humanoid. A separate safety layer limits joint position, velocity, and torque, and stops the robot if its state estimate is stale or the emergency stop is pressed or disconnected. In balance-loss trials using a model-predictive lower-body controller, the robot did not recover and the operator had to stop it; removing balance control caused a fall. The authors argue for staged force authority with explicit human or organizational responsibility.
summary.zh: 本文介绍用于 Unitree H1-2 人形机器人的开源自主系统安全机制及部署经验。独立安全层对关节位置、速度和力矩设限，并在状态估计过期或急停被按下、断开时停止机器人。作者让站立机器人失去平衡；使用模型预测下肢控制器时，机器人均未能恢复，每次都需操作员急停，而急停会移除平衡控制并导致跌倒。作者指出，面向操作任务设定的限值在正常行走时也会触发停止，跌倒在操作员或电池组附近可能更危险。文章据此主张分阶段授予机器人施力权限，并明确由个人或组织承担责任。

sections.text:
Aerial robots operating in cluttered environments may encounter openings narrower than their nominal width. Existing passively morphing drones reduce their width upon traversal, but they typically involve human-made designs, which can struggle to find the right balance among folding ratio, flight efficiency, and control tracking performance.

We introduce a closed-loop design method that jointly optimizes quadrotor geometry and the torque-deflection response of two passively folding arms driven by the success rate in simulation for contact-mediated gap traversal.

An optimization algorithm samples candidate designs that are evaluated in a contact-based simulation of the traversal task, where the task success rate is used as a feedback signal to sample progressively better designs over time.

The resulting prototype passively reduces its width from 31.3 to 14.1 cm and traverses a 15 cm wide opening at a 2 m/s reference speed. It also tolerates gap approach-angle errors of up to 30 degrees and folds through a 40 cm long confined passage.

Compared to a rigid twin, the soft configuration adds only 2 mm of position RMSE and less than 1% electrical power during contact-free flight. These results show that task-driven closed-loop design optimization can produce passively morphing airframes that are compact under contact, tolerant to approach error, and effectively rigid during nominal flight.

summary.en: The paper presents a closed-loop method that jointly optimizes quadrotor geometry and the torque-deflection response of two passively folding arms, using simulated success in contact-mediated gap traversal as feedback. Candidate designs are evaluated in contact-based simulation. The resulting prototype narrows from 31.3 to 14.1 cm and traverses a 15 cm opening at a 2 m/s reference speed, tolerating approach-angle errors up to 30 degrees and a 40 cm confined passage. Compared with a rigid twin, contact-free flight adds 2 mm position RMSE and less than 1% electrical power.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种闭环设计优化方法，联合优化四旋翼的几何形状及两条被动折叠机臂的力矩—偏转响应，以仿真中的接触式窄缝穿越成功率作为反馈。算法在接触仿真中评估候选设计，并据此逐步采样改进方案。所得原型可将宽度从31.3厘米缩至14.1厘米，在参考速度2米/秒时穿过15厘米开口，且能容忍最高30度的接近角误差、通过40厘米长的狭窄通道。与刚性对照机相比，无接触飞行时位置均方根误差仅增加2毫米，电功率增加不到1%。

sections.text:
Recent years have seen a focus on research into distributed optimization algorithms for multi-robot Collaborative Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (C-SLAM).Research in this domain, however, is made difficult by a lack of standard benchmark datasets.

Such datasets have been used to great effect in the field of single-robot SLAM, and researchers focused on multi-robot problems would benefit greatly from dedicated benchmark datasets.

To address this gap, we design and release the Collaborative Open-Source Multi-robot Optimization Benchmark (COSMO-Bench) -- a suite of 24 datasets derived from a baseline C-SLAM front-end and real-world LiDAR data. Data DOI: https://doi.org/10.1184/R1/29652158

summary.en: The paper addresses the lack of standard benchmark datasets for research on distributed optimization in multi-robot Collaborative SLAM. It presents and releases COSMO-Bench, a benchmark suite containing 24 datasets derived from a baseline C-SLAM front end and real-world LiDAR data. The abstract describes the dataset resource and its motivation but does not report benchmark evaluation results.

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform versatile manipulation tasks from language instructions, but their inference cost limits how fast a robot can respond in closed-loop control.

Visual token pruning reduces this cost; however, prior methods estimate token redundancy from encoded visual embeddings or attention, only after the visual encoder has processed the entire observation.

We propose ActPrune, a training-free token pruning method that moves the pruning decision ahead of the vision encoder by grounding it in a geometric prior derived from the robot's own action.

The action chunk predicted at the previous control step is already available before the current observation is encoded, and it specifies the end-effector and camera motion between consecutive observations.

The same action affects the two standard camera views asymmetrically: in the fixed third-person view, ActPrune retains patches along the projected end-effector trajectory together with semantic anchors, while in the wrist view, it prunes patches that remain unchanged after compensating for the action-induced camera motion.

Extensive experiments on two simulation environments (LIBERO and VLABench) and four real-robot tasks demonstrate that ActPrune achieves up to 1.61$\times$ speedup and 59.5% FLOPs reduction with negligible degradation in success rates. The project site is http://mmai.ewha.ac.kr/actprune/.

summary.en: ActPrune is a training-free visual token pruning method that uses the robot's predicted action from the previous control step to decide what to retain before the current observation enters the vision encoder. It handles fixed third-person and wrist-camera views differently, preserving projected end-effector trajectories and semantic anchors in one, and pruning unchanged wrist-view patches after compensating for action-induced camera motion. Experiments in two simulation environments and four real-robot tasks reportedly achieved up to 1.61× speedup and 59.5% fewer FLOPs with negligible success-rate degradation.
summary.zh: 本文提出无需训练的视觉令牌剪枝方法 ActPrune，利用机器人前一控制步预测的动作，在当前观测送入视觉编码器前决定保留或剪除哪些图像块。该动作描述末端执行器和相机的运动；方法针对固定第三人称视角保留末端轨迹投影区域及语义锚点，并在腕部视角剪除补偿动作引起相机运动后保持不变的区域。作者报告，在两个仿真环境和四项真实机器人任务中，该方法最高实现1.61倍加速和59.5% FLOPs削减，成功率仅有可忽略的下降。

sections.text:
Recent advances in frontier models have pushed the boundaries of agentic robot control, enabling agents to perform complex robotic tasks through reasoning and interaction. However, repeated calls to these models during execution can substantially increase task completion time.

Code as Policies (CaP) offers a route for coding agents to acquire physical skills through experience and retain them in executable programs, allowing the reasoning invested in development to be reused across runs. Developing reliable code policies while limiting the cost of physical experimentation remains a central challenge.

We investigate human guidance as a source of priors for feasible actions and simulation as an auxiliary environment for exploring and testing candidate policies. Our findings favor robot demonstrations available on request and simulation used selectively during real-world policy refinement.

These findings inform ACE-CaP-0, an agentic recipe that couples policy revision with experience acquisition through Demonstrations on Request and Simulation on Demand. Across eight real-world manipulation tasks spanning alignment, multi-object handling, and bimanual coordination, the resulting frozen programs achieve 92.1\% success (221/240 trials).

Mean execution times across tasks range from 0.97 to 2.27 minutes. The programs execute with runtime perception and control, without a human or coding agent in the loop. These results highlight CaP's potential to turn experience into reliable, reusable physical skills.

summary.en: The paper studies how human guidance and simulation can reduce the cost of developing code-based robot policies, and introduces ACE-CaP-0, which combines policy revision with demonstrations and simulation used on demand. Across eight real-world manipulation tasks involving alignment, multiple objects, and bimanual coordination, the resulting frozen programs achieved 92.1% success (221/240 trials). Mean execution times ranged from 0.97 to 2.27 minutes. The programs used runtime perception and control without a human or coding agent in the loop.

sections.text:
Collaborative Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (C-SLAM) is a fundamental capability for multi-robot teams as it enables downstream tasks like planning and navigation.

However, existing C-SLAM back-end algorithms that are required to solve this problem struggle to address the practical realities of real-world deployments (i.e. communication limitations, outlier measurements, and online operation).

In this paper we propose Robust Incremental Manifold Edge-based Separable ADMM (riMESA) -- a robust, incremental, and distributed C-SLAM back-end that is resilient to outliers, reliable in the face of limited communication, and can compute accurate state estimates for a multi-robot team in real-time.

Through the development of riMESA, we, more broadly, make an argument for the use of Consensus Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers as a theoretical foundation for distributed optimization tasks in robotics like C-SLAM due to its flexibility, accuracy, and fast convergence.

We conclude this work with an in-depth evaluation of riMESA on a variety of C-SLAM problem scenarios and communication network conditions using both synthetic and real-world C-SLAM data.

These experiments demonstrate that riMESA is able to generalize across conditions, produce accurate state estimates, operate in real-time, and outperform the accuracy of prior works by a factor >7x on real-world datasets.

summary.en: The paper proposes riMESA, a robust, incremental, distributed back end for collaborative SLAM, designed to handle communication limits, outlier measurements, and online operation while estimating multi-robot states in real time. The authors also argue that Consensus ADMM provides a useful theoretical foundation for distributed robotics optimization. Their evaluation covers varied C-SLAM scenarios and network conditions using synthetic and real-world data. They report generalization across conditions, real-time operation, accurate state estimates, and accuracy more than seven times that of prior work on real-world datasets.
summary.zh: 论文提出 riMESA，一种面向多机器人协同定位与建图后端的鲁棒、增量式分布式算法，旨在应对通信受限、离群测量和在线运行等实际条件，并实时计算团队状态估计。作者进一步主张，Consensus ADMM 可作为机器人分布式优化任务的理论基础。评估覆盖多种协同建图场景和通信网络条件，使用合成数据与真实数据。作者报告实验显示该方法能跨条件泛化、实时运行并产生准确状态估计；在真实数据集上的准确性超过既有工作的七倍。

items.title: riMESA: Consensus ADMM for Real-World Collaborative SLAM

sections.text:
Planning for a heterogeneous robot team from a scene image and an instruction involves two kinds of decisions. Some must be judged from the scene: which goals are already met, how the task splits, and which robot does what. Others follow from these and can be computed: prerequisite actions, handoffs between robots, and timing.

We argue that each kind should go to the component suited to it: a small vision-language model learns the first, and a deterministic solver computes the second. In NSDL (Neuro-Symbolic Division of Labor), the trained model writes its judgments as a plan sketch, which lists the goals that still need action and the intended steps in order, each with a robot.

The solver expands the sketch into an executable joint plan. The model calls two tools, a detector for evidence and the solver, and is trained with the solver in the loop. We evaluate on the public VIKI-L2 benchmark and on LOCUS-Bench, a new benchmark that grades the two kinds of difficulty separately.

NSDL outperforms end-to-end planners and formalize-then-plan baselines on both benchmarks and with three backbones from 3B to 8B; the 7B model reaches 97.0% out-of-distribution accuracy on VIKI-L2.

Ordering and scheduling errors nearly disappear once the solver writes the structure; the remaining failures are misjudged states, and most goals the model misses are ones it never lists. Code, model weights, and LOCUS-Bench are publicly available at https://github.com/Xincheng-Tan/NSDL.

summary.en: NSDL divides multi-robot planning into scene-dependent judgments and decisions that a solver can compute. A small vision-language model identifies completed goals, task allocation, and robot assignments in a plan sketch; a deterministic solver expands it into an executable joint plan. The authors evaluate the approach on VIKI-L2 and LOCUS-Bench and report that it outperforms end-to-end planners and formalize-then-plan baselines. The 7B model reaches 97.0% out-of-distribution accuracy on VIKI-L2. Once the solver supplies the structure, remaining failures mainly involve state judgments.
summary.zh: NSDL 将多机器人规划中的决策分为依赖场景判断的部分和可由求解器计算的部分：小型视觉语言模型判断已完成目标、任务分工及机器人分配，并写出计划草图；确定性求解器据此生成可执行的联合计划。作者在 VIKI-L2 和 LOCUS-Bench 上评估，报告称该方法优于端到端规划器及形式化后规划基线；7B 模型在 VIKI-L2 上的分布外准确率为 97.0%。求解器生成结构后，主要剩余错误来自状态判断。

items.title: NSDL: Neuro-Symbolic Division of Labor for Multi-Robot Task Planning

We present Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. MR0 combines 147 million vision-language samples with 15,060 hours of curated robot trajectories spanning 12 embodiments.

A three-stage training recipe aligns multimodal representations with robot behavior through discrete action-token pre-training, transfers these priors to continuous cross-embodiment control through flow-matching mid-training, and adapts the policy through real-world post-training.

We introduce Rollback, which pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections to provide positive and negative supervision for CFG-DAgger without value learning or advantage labeling. A unified end-effector interface supports heterogeneous embodiments, while asynchronous action-chunk merging maintains smooth execution under variable inference latency.

An event-driven agent maintains persistent task events and reassesses plans when progress or feasibility changes, enabling cross-task retrieval and conditional task resumption. MR0 achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ranks fifth in the RoboDojo VLA track.

Under matched HG-DAgger post-training, MR0 achieves higher average success rate and progress score than $\pi_{0.5}$ across three real-robot tasks. On Ethernet insertion, CFG-DAgger trained with Rollback data reaches 70% success and a progress score of 0.90.

Qualitative agent deployments demonstrate cross-task event retrieval and recovery from temporarily unsatisfied task conditions.

summary.en: Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0) is a vision-language-action model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation, trained with vision-language samples and robot trajectories from 12 embodiments. Its methods include staged training, Rollback supervision that pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections, a unified end-effector interface, and asynchronous action-chunk merging. An event-driven agent tracks task progress and reassesses plans when conditions change. The authors report 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and fifth place in the RoboDojo VLA track. Results on real-robot tasks and Ethernet insertion reflect the specific training and evaluation settings described.

sections.text:
Large language models (LLMs) can supply autonomous systems with plans, predictions, and judgments, but these contributions are sometimes wrong. This review asks how a system can maximize an LLM's utility while managing its fallibility. Our answer is to adapt the system's reliance on the LLM as evidence about the LLM's performance accumulates.

Systems built from imperfect components, such as noisy sensors and faulty software, have long worked in this way, and the classical methods they use can be applied to LLM-based systems as well. A system can change its reliance on an LLM in several ways, depending on the LLM's role and on the other components in the system.

Each change needs an estimate of the LLM's reliability, and the LLM's role and the kind of contribution it makes determine what to estimate. Classical methods from decision theory, estimation, and online learning then turn these estimates into reliance decisions. These decisions can reduce how often LLM errors affect the system.

However, some errors matter even when they are rare. An independently verified mechanism can prevent such errors from being executed. Without one, adapting reliance using reliability estimates can still keep their risk within a bound.

Studies on adapting reliance on LLMs are emerging but limited, and the reviewed comparisons suggest that adapting reliance can improve system performance.

summary.en: This review examines how autonomous systems can use large language models for plans, predictions, and judgments while managing errors. The authors propose adapting reliance on an LLM as evidence about its performance accumulates, estimating reliability according to the model’s role, and using methods from decision theory, estimation, and online learning to guide reliance decisions. Independently verified mechanisms can prevent rare but consequential errors from being executed. Without such mechanisms, reliability-based adaptation can still keep risk within a bound. The review says research remains limited, while existing comparisons suggest adaptive reliance may improve system performance.
summary.zh: 这篇综述讨论如何在利用大型语言模型提供计划、预测和判断的同时管理其错误。作者主张，系统应根据不断积累的性能证据调整对模型的依赖，并依据模型承担的角色估计其可靠性，再用决策理论、估计和在线学习方法作出依赖决策。对于虽少见但后果严重的错误，可由独立验证机制阻止执行；若没有该机制，可靠性估计仍可用于将风险控制在界限内。综述指出相关研究仍有限，但现有比较显示调整依赖可能改善系统表现。

sections.text:
Motion imitation enables humanoid robots to acquire whole-body skills such as walking and dancing. However, fine-tuning an entire policy for a new skill can affect existing behaviors, while training a separate policy for each skill increases training and maintenance costs.

We present PERA, a method for learning new skills by reusing existing motion capabilities. PERA freezes a pretrained mixture-of-experts policy and trains an additional task expert and its routing score using task rewards or teacher-action supervision.

In Unitree G1 simulation, each added task module contains approximately 1.03% of the parameters of the base actor. Built on our pretrained policy, PERA successfully completes all ten new tasks. Disabling the expert restores the original computation path of the base policy, which still fully executes all 126 original motions.

Enabling the expert also improves the execution of some dance motions not used to train that expert, indicating that its benefits extend beyond its training motions. Experiments with HoloMotion further demonstrate the applicability of PERA to different base policies.

summary.en: The paper presents PERA, which freezes a pretrained mixture-of-experts policy and adds a task expert and routing score, trained with task rewards or teacher-action supervision. In Unitree G1 simulation, each added module contains about 1.03% of the base actor's parameters, and PERA completes ten new tasks. With the expert disabled, the base policy still executes its original 126 motions. The authors also report improvements on some untrained dance motions and applicability to different base policies using HoloMotion.
